note: [agent-bulk] mcp2k other_em, the busy one: 49 segments, 31 showers, 7 in scope (27016, 100074, 80031, 101086, 88047, 91056, 95062). The other 24 are all under 20 MeV and I did not look at them individually; everything below is a claim about the leading shower and about the event's geometry, NOT about 31 showers. drag_check both true, probe 307.2 px off centroid, not degenerate. r95 222.5 cm so the default vertex sweep framed at +-278 cm was useless for the vertex; I judged the vertex from a --vtx-span 60 re-capture (shots-vtx/evt167612), at two azimuths. WHY THIS IS A VERTEX RESULT. The main vertex is 195-215 cm away from every piece of electromagnetic activity in the event. At +-60 cm the star sits on ONE object and nothing else: it is the kink between 26001 (55.4 cm, pdg 2212, 93 points) and 26002 (6.5 cm, pdg 13) -- a single track that bends, both halves correctly unowned -- and there is no other prong and no shower stem anywhere within 60 cm of it, at either azimuth. Everything the scan cares about is in a separate blob 190-215 cm away: 27016 (200.4 MeV), 100074 (91.8), 101086 (36.2), 88047 (34.9) and a dozen smaller showers. Between the two there is only a sprinkle of isolated 0.3 cm two-point specks out to 116 cm and then a 75 cm hole. A photon travelling 200 cm before converting is an e^-8 proposition on a 25 cm conversion length, and here it would have to happen twice. So the star is not the origin of this EM system. WHAT I CANNOT DECIDE, which is why this bucket says undecidable: either the main vertex is misplaced and the real neutrino vertex is inside the EM blob -- the reconstruction has 82 vertices in this event and at least eight of them sit within 9 cm of the leading shower's start -- or the main vertex is right and the whole EM blob is a separate object (a cosmic-induced shower, say) that the clustering wrongly pulled into the same neutrino candidate. The cloud banner says 5 of 27 clusters carry the reconstruction (ids 14, 24, 25, 26, 27), i.e. both the lone track (cluster 26) and the EM blob (cluster 27) are inside the candidate. I cannot separate those two readings from the display. SECOND, INDEPENDENT FINDING -- start/axis wrong. Shower 27016 (200.4 MeV, 8 seg, 70.7 cm) has a badly fitted axis and a badly placed start, and this would be my verdict if the vertex question were settled. Its own cmp_div says its members span 0.0 to 72.9 deg from its axis: 27018 at 45.1 deg, 27019 at 60.0, 27015 at 60.3, 27010 at 61.0, 27017 at 72.9. At az-055 the orange axis arrow points almost perpendicular to the direction the member set actually extends, and the X sits in the MIDDLE of the member chain rather than at either end -- the chain runs both left and right of it, out to a junction from which two arms leave. The same mid-chain start shows at az+085, 140 deg away. Whether the wide member spread is over-clustering (two arms of a junction being one shower) or an honest shower fan I could not settle, and the wrong axis makes the angle column unusable for deciding it, which is exactly why I am not recording an over-clustering verdict off it. NO UNDER-CLUSTERING that I can see: there is no grey unowned charge anywhere near 27016; the dozen small objects at 8-42 cm from it (96063, 92059, 90055, 97064, 89054, 91056, 88047, 100074's six segments, 101086, 95062, 94089) are every one of them owned by their own sub-showers, and they sit at 44-107 deg where the axis is not to be trusted anyway. I ran the correction-11 reconciliation on 27016 -- owner-grouped count 8, cmp_div says 8 -- so its membership is what the table says. PI0: no reco pi0 group. The display auto-slotted 27016 + 100074 and this is the clearest illustration in my shard of why the two conventions must not be merged: the axis convention gives theta 46.6 deg -> 107.2 MeV and calls it in the accept window, while the vertex convention gives theta 7.0 deg -> 16.5 MeV, a factor of 6.5, purely because the 200 cm lever arm from the misplaced star makes the two lines of sight nearly parallel. Neither number means anything until the vertex question above is answered. kine_pio_* separately reports 13.2 MeV from 27016 + a 16.2 MeV object; that is a BDT feature over all pairs and I did not read it as a pairing.

[agent-bulk] mcp2k numucc_em WITH an ACCEPTED reco pi0 group, and the pi0 is the finding here, not the clustering. 18 segments, 10 showers, 2 in scope (9005, 24018); the eight skipped (25020, 23015, 26021, 14010, 21013, 27022, 35023, 19011) are 1.0 cm and smaller and I did not look at them. drag_check both true, probe 342.9 px off centroid, not degenerate. r95 184.2 cm because of a 164 cm muon, so the default sweep was framed at +-184 cm; I judged the vertex from a --vtx-span 60 re-capture (shots-vtx/evt171729). VERTEX is good: at +-60 cm the star sits at the end of segment 9001 (164.1 cm, pdg 13, 272 points, correctly unowned) with two things leaving it -- the 5.8 cm pdg-2212 stub 9008 (also correctly unowned) and shower 9005. CLUSTERING of the leading shower 9005 (117.2 MeV, 4 seg, conn 1, pio_id 0): its four members (9005 seed 15.4 cm, 9007 at 12.0 cm / 9.7 deg, 9009 at 13.3 cm / 3.3 deg, 20012 at 16.3 cm / 21.9 deg) are contiguous and cover the visible object, which at az-055 and again at el+65 is a genuinely diffuse fan of charge spreading out from the star -- not a line. The straightness numbers agree it is EM and not a track: the seed has chord 13.3 cm, path 15.4 cm (wiggle 1.156) with a 1.60 cm transverse excursion, and 9009 has wiggle 1.912, against 1.019 for the proton at the same vertex and 1.063 for the 164 cm muon. Nothing unowned sits in front of it: the only non-members inside 45 cm and 70 deg are 23015 (0.4 cm at 30.0 cm / 28.9 deg) and 21013 (0.3 cm at 31.8 cm / 66.8 deg), both negligible specks, and everything else is at 119-139 deg, i.e. behind. Correction-11 reconciliation run: owner-grouped count 4, cmp_div says 4. So I record correct on the clustering. THE PI0, and this is why the event is worth the owner's eye. Reco group 0 pairs 9005 + 24018 and stores 118.9 MeV, right in the accept window. But GAMMA 1 IS ON THE NEUTRINO VERTEX: kine_div prints gamma1's start as (-9.1, 127.8, 291.1), which is the main vertex to the last digit, its seed 9005 has 0.0 cm closest approach to the star, and it is in cluster 9, the same cluster as the muon and the proton. A converted photon cannot start at zero conversion length -- that is the evt280159 pattern from the pilot, except that there the reconstruction's pairing was merely proposed and here it is an ACCEPTED group carrying a mass. The consequence is visible in the pricing: the vertex convention cannot even be evaluated (gamma1 has no chord from the vertex, kine_div prints theta '-' and m '-'), so the only number that exists is the axis convention's theta 146.5 deg -> 130.7 MeV, which lands 4 MeV from the pi0 mass and looks like a beautiful pi0 while resting entirely on a gamma that is sitting on the vertex. GAMMA 2 by contrast is a good photon: 24018 (39.8 MeV) is detached by 24.5 cm, its own diffuse blob, clearly separated in the +-60 cm frame. So my reading is that this is a real photon paired with vertex EM activity. I did NOT store the pairing, deliberately -- storing it would read as endorsement, and I am disputing it, not proposing an alternative (there is no third EM object above 20 MeV in this event to pair 24018 with). WHAT WOULD OVERTURN THIS: if the 117 MeV blob on the vertex is itself a pi0 whose two gammas both converted within a centimetre or two, then the reconstruction is right that there is a pi0 here and only wrong about which objects the gammas are. I cannot separate that from the display. kine_pio_* independently reports 118.9 MeV at 128.1 deg from the same two showers; I checked it separately from pio_id and did not merge them.

[agent-bulk] mcp2k numucc_em, sparse: 14 segments, 6 showers, ONE in scope (17012); the five skipped (17007, 115017, 20014, 113015, 114016) are 3.8 cm and smaller. drag_check both true, probe 225.2 px off centroid, not degenerate. r95 240.8 cm so the default sweep framed at +-301 cm; I judged the vertex from a --vtx-span 60 re-capture (shots-vtx/evt179048). WHY VERTEX-BAD. At +-60 cm the star sits ON a single continuous straight line of charge that passes straight through it and runs off both edges of the frame. Nothing converges there. I measured the directions from the star rather than trusting the picture: taking the far end of 17009 as the reference axis, 17012 leaves at 3.2 deg, 17010 at 4-8 deg, 17008 at 7-8 deg, 17009 at 0-8 deg out to 246 cm, and 17003/17001 at 1-2 deg out to 249 cm -- while 17013 (63.5 cm, pdg 13) leaves at 176.4 deg, i.e. anti-parallel to within 3.6 deg. So the whole event is ONE straight object about 311 cm long with the star 62 cm from one end. The only thing at the star that is not collinear is 17011, a 9.6 cm pdg-211 stub whose far end is at 33.4 deg, which is as consistent with a delta ray off a passing muon as with a vertex prong. Reading (a): this is a through-going cosmic muon and the neutrino vertex is spurious. Reading (b): it is a genuine interaction with a 249 cm forward track and a 62 cm backward track that happen to be back-to-back to 3.6 deg. I cannot separate them, which is what this bucket is for. THE SECOND FINDING, and it does NOT depend on the vertex, because it is measured from the shower's own start: shower 17012 (137.9 MeV, 6 seg) has members spanning 0.0 to 247.9 cm -- its own cmp_div says so. Its near members (17012 seed 28.1 cm, 17010 7.8 cm at 27.1 cm, 17030 1.3 cm at 27.6 cm) sit at the star, and then 17003 (8.2 cm) and 17001 (1.3 cm) are members at 246.2 and 247.9 cm, at the FAR END of the line, while the entire 213 cm in between -- segment 17009, 221.1 cm, 369 points -- is correctly left unowned. A 138 MeV electromagnetic shower cannot be 248 cm long; it has reached across a through-going track and claimed the far end. I have marked 17003 and 17001 OUT of 17012. Both marks are strong; neither is the weak kind correction 7 asks me to flag. WHAT I ALSO BELIEVE BUT DID NOT RECORD AS THE VERDICT: this object is not an EM shower at all. The seed 17012 has chord 27.6 cm, path 28.1 cm (wiggle 1.021) and a 0.54 cm maximum transverse excursion, which is the same straightness as the 63.5 cm muon beside it (1.021) and the 221 cm track it reaches across (1.037); it is a MIP segment, not a shower. So all three of vertex-bad, over-clustered and not-an-EM-shower are defensible on this event; I followed the brief's rubric and judged the vertex first, and the OUT marks carry the over-clustering statement so it is not lost. PI0: no reco pi0 group, no second EM object above 20 MeV, and the display could not even auto-slot a pair (pio.slots is null), so there is no mass to report.

[agent-bulk] mcp2k NUECC, compact: everything in the event sits within 40 cm of the star (r95 gives a half-span of only 48.7 cm, so the default vertex sweep is legible and no --vtx-span re-capture was needed). 22 segments, 14 showers, 4 in scope (11037, 11038, 56030, 58032); the ten skipped (57031, 40012, 45017, 44016, 39011, 42014, 41013, 15010, 61035, 46018) are all under 20 MeV, and several of them are part of the ambiguity below, so read this as a claim about 11037 and not about the event. drag_check both true, probe 334.9 px off centroid, not degenerate. VERTEX is good: two prongs leave the star and only two -- 11037 (22.2 cm, pdg 11, the electron candidate) and 11038 (14.9 cm, pdg 211) -- and at el+60 they still converge cleanly on it. For a nuecc event an EM object starting AT the vertex is exactly what is expected, so unlike the numucc events in my shard the zero-conversion-length start is not a red flag here. LEADING SHOWER 11037 (105.6 MeV, 4 seg, 37.1 cm, conn 1): its four members (11037 seed, 11007 at 16.4 cm / 9.1 deg, 11006 at 19.4 cm / 7.9 deg, 11009 at 22.2 cm / 4.5 deg) are contiguous, one apex, one direction, with a diffuse branching cloud around them that looks properly electromagnetic from both az-055 and az+085. By the brief's definition of under-clustering -- charge contiguous with the member set, small angle to the axis, within or just beyond the member spread -- nothing qualifies, so I record correct. WHY THE CONFIDENCE IS UNCLEAR, and this is the substance of the entry. There is about 77 MeV of other EM-labelled charge sitting 7 to 15 cm from this electron's start, and I could not decide whether it belongs to it: 56030 (45.8 MeV, with 56029) at 14.0-14.6 cm, 58032 (21.3 MeV) at 6.8 cm, 57031 (with 60034 and 59033) at 7.0 cm. If they belong, the electron is roughly 180 MeV rather than 106 and the event is badly under-clustered; if they do not, this is ordinary hadronic activity at a nuecc vertex that happens to carry a pdg-11 label. THE TWO READINGS AND WHY THEY DO NOT SEPARATE: against inclusion, all of them sit at 93-118 deg to 11037's axis, which is nearly transverse, and none of them appears anywhere in the pass-1 acceptance window because that plot's angle axis stops near 15 deg here. For inclusion, 7-15 cm is inside one Moliere radius in liquid argon (~9.5 cm), which is exactly where a 100 MeV shower's wide-angle charge lives, and it is right at the shower start where the lateral spread is largest. The display shows angle to the axis but not transverse profile, and I cannot separate 'Moliere-radius shower charge' from 'hadronic vertex blob' by eye. THE ONE THING THE ACCEPTANCE PLOT DOES SHOW: exactly one non-member circle, 47019 (3.9 cm, cluster 47) at 38.4 cm / 7.1 deg, on-axis and well inside the 12.5 deg step, currently owned by 11038 (the pdg-211 shower) via pass3_cone. I ran the correction-11 reconciliation before treating it as a genuine non-member: 11037's owner-grouped count is 4 and its cmp_div says 4, and 11038's owner-grouped count is 3 and its nseg is 3, so 47019 really is exclusively 11038's and this is not a dual-membership artifact. I did NOT mark it in, because it fails the other half of the brief's rule: 11037's members stop at 22.2 cm and 47019 is at 38.4 cm with an empty 15 cm gap in between, so it is neither contiguous nor 'just beyond' the member spread. It is on-axis for the electron and it was accepted into a pion by a cone cut, which is the kind of thing worth a second opinion. PI0: no reco pi0 group, and I would not propose one -- the display auto-slotted 11037 + 56030, but 11037 starts on the vertex so the vertex convention has no chord (kine_div prints theta '-'), and the axis convention's 69.6 deg -> 80.1 MeV pairs the electron with a blob 14 cm away, which is not a photon pair. For a nuecc event the absence of a pi0 group is the right answer.

[agent-bulk] mcp2k numucc_em. 40 segments, 15 showers, 2 in scope (63034, 77063); the thirteen skipped are 1.6 cm and smaller and I did not look at them individually, though several are named below as non-members. drag_check both true, probe 206.2 px off centroid, not degenerate. r95 223.1 cm because of a 100 cm muon, so the default sweep was framed at +-223 cm; I judged the vertex from a --vtx-span 60 re-capture (shots-vtx/evt289246). VERTEX is good: at +-60 cm the star is a clean two-prong V and nothing else -- 16001 (100.7 cm, pdg 13, 169 points) one way and 16002 (15.9 cm, pdg 2212) the other, both correctly unowned. THE UNDER-CLUSTERING. Shower 63034 (264.0 MeV, 23 segments, conn 2) is a large, well-populated, clearly electromagnetic complex: its 23 members run 0 to 62.9 cm from its start at 0.0 to 21.3 deg, and its acceptance plot shows all 23 squares and NO non-member circle anywhere in the window out to 80 cm and 27 deg. What it is missing sits off the TOP of that plot: 77063 (2.5 cm) and 77064 (8.0 cm) -- one 38.2 MeV object, 10.5 cm of segment -- at 14.7 and 15.3 cm from 63034's start and 53.0 and 46.7 deg from its axis. I ran the correction-11 reconciliation before calling this: 63034's owner-grouped count is 23 and its cmp_div says 23, and 77063's owner-grouped count is 2 and its nseg is 2, so this is genuine non-membership and not the first-owner-wins artifact. THE ARGUMENT, and it is a transverse-radius argument rather than an angle one: at 15 cm and 50 deg the missing object is about 11.5 cm off the shower axis, and 63034 already accepts members at 20.9-21.3 deg at 25-30 cm, which is 9-11 cm off the same axis. So the shower's own accepted transverse reach is the same 11 cm; the piece is rejected only because it sits closer to the start, where the same transverse offset subtends a much larger angle. That is what a pure angular cone cut does near a shower start, and in liquid argon 11 cm is about 1.2 Moliere radii on a 264 MeV shower, i.e. exactly where the last ~10 percent of the energy lives. Adding it moves the shower from 264 to 302 MeV. THE WEAKNESS, and it is why this is likely rather than certain: 47-53 deg is a large angle to defend on a picture, and at az+085 the missing object reads as a compact blob beside the shower start rather than as an obvious part of the body. It is NOT a second photon: the display auto-slotted 63034 + 77063 and the vertex convention gives theta 1.1 deg -> 2.0 MeV and the axis convention theta 17.5 deg -> 30.6 MeV, i.e. the two objects lie in the same direction from the star (130 and 145 cm out) and cannot be a pi0 pair. That collinearity from the vertex is itself an argument that they are one object. A SEPARATE THING WORTH THE OWNER'S EYE, which I did not turn into the verdict: 63034 starts 130.2 cm from the neutrino vertex, 89.1 cm beyond the end of the 100.7 cm muon and at 43 deg to the muon direction. For a photon that is about five conversion lengths in liquid argon, a sub-percent proposition, so either this is a rare long conversion, or the 264 MeV shower does not belong to this neutrino interaction at all. The vertex itself is unambiguous (two prongs converge on it), so I did not record vertex-bad; but the association between that vertex and this shower is the weakest link in the event. PI0: no reco pi0 group, and none should be expected -- there is no second EM object in the event that is not part of 63034.

[agent-bulk] mcp2k numucc_em, 32 showers, scope rule reaches 5 (57050, 24030, 37038, 58051, 65058); the other 27 are all 10.2 MeV and below and I did not look at them. VERTEX: r95 was 296.8 cm so the default sweep framed the vertex at +-297 cm and was unusable; I judged the vertex from a --vtx-span 60 re-capture (shots-vtx/evt54453). At +-60 cm the star sits cleanly on the upstream end of one object: segment 22010 (cluster 22, pdg 13, 31.5 cm, 53 points) leaves the star with 0.0 cm closest approach and runs out to 30 cm, continued by 22016 (11.7 cm, pdg 2212) and 22018 (6.6 cm) to 39 cm. All of cluster 22 is correctly left unowned. Vertex is good, so this is a clustering call, not a vertex call. LEADING SHOWER 57050 (198.8 MeV, 4 seg, 33.8 cm, conn 2, pio_id -1): its start X is 45.6 cm from the star, i.e. a detached conversion beyond the muon stem, and its member set (57050 seed 11.5 cm, 23025 19.3 cm, 23027 2.7 cm, 66059 0.4 cm) is one connected object with a clear kink at the shower maximum, visible at az-055/el+65 as a junction from which several prongs radiate into a broad point cloud. UNDER-CLUSTERING, and the strong half of it is grey: 23028 (cluster 23, 6.3 cm, 12 points) is owned by NO shower at all, sits 9.4 cm from 57050's start, and is a sibling of 57050's own two largest members 23025 and 23027, which are also cluster 23. The weaker half, and the one I would let the owner reverse: 23026 (cluster 23, 13.0 cm, 23 points) is owned by 58051, a 31.5 MeV shower whose own seed segment is only 4.9 cm long -- a 13 cm segment hanging off a 5 cm seed, in the big shower's own cluster. I ran the correction-11 reconciliation test rather than reading the owner column: 57050's owner-grouped count is 4 and its cmp_div says 4 segments, and 58051's owner-grouped count is 2 and its cmp_div says 2, so 23026 is genuinely NOT a dual member of 57050 -- the neighbour really does hold it exclusively. THE CAVEAT that keeps this at likely and not certain: both marked segments read 59.5 deg to 57050's axis at 9.4 cm, which is a transverse offset of about 8 cm. That is inside one Moliere radius in LAr (~9.5 cm) and so physically belongs, but it is far outside the pass-1 acceptance window -- 57050's acceptance plot has NO non-member circle anywhere in it, because the plot's angle axis stops near 34 deg and these sit off the top of it. So the corroboration the brief asks for (a circle just outside a dashed step) is absent by construction here, and the case rests on the grey segment plus the cluster identity. NOT MARKED, but worth naming: 66059 (0.4 cm, pdg 13) is a member at 31.4 cm / 26.8 deg absorbed by pass4_angle, a long reach for negligible charge; and 65058 (23.1 MeV) is a scattered object whose four members run 0-46.4 cm and include three 0.2-0.4 cm stubs picked up by in_other_clusters_seg_cone at 45, 50 and 77 cm from the vertex -- I did not record a verdict on it. PI0: no reco pi0 group (all pio_id -1). The display auto-slotted 57050 + 24030 (106.6 MeV, detached 87.3 cm from the star), which is the only plausible pair in the event, and it does NOT price as a pi0 in either convention: vertex convention theta 34.9 deg -> m 87.3 MeV, axis convention theta 139.3 deg -> m 273.0 MeV. So this event is not the both-conventions-accept case; it is a photon pair that is either not a pi0 or has a badly measured opening angle. The kine_pio_* block reports mass 12.0 from 57050 + 58051 at 8.7 deg, which is a BDT feature over all candidate pairs and not a pairing -- I did not read it as one.

[agent-bulk] mcp2k numucc_em, sparse: 12 segments, 6 showers, only 2 in scope (20021, 20019); the four skipped ones (60016, 29013, 61017, 59015) are 3.9 cm and shorter and I did not look at them. drag_check both true, probe 168.7 px off centroid, not degenerate. VERTEX: r95 264.0 cm because of a 230.8 cm muon, so the default sweep was framed at +-264 cm and unusable; I judged the vertex from a --vtx-span 60 re-capture (shots-vtx/evt69232). At +-60 cm the star sits at one END of segment 20011 (cluster 20, pdg 13, 230.8 cm, 386 points, correctly unowned) with three other prongs leaving the same point: 20022 (26.6 cm, pdg 211, unowned), 20021 (27.5 cm, the leading shower's seed) and 20019 (8.0 cm, the 22.7 MeV shower). Four prongs converging on the star, so the vertex is good and this is a clustering call. THE FINDING, and it is what the +-60 cm framing shows: the star sits at the point where a thin MIP line becomes a shower. Above the star the muon is a ~1 cm wide straight line; below it the charge cloud widens progressively into a blob at 30-45 cm. The reconstruction has drawn a 195.2 MeV EM shower over BOTH halves of that transition: its seed, segment 20021, starts at 0.0 cm from the ν vertex and runs 27.5 cm as a very straight minimum-ionising line -- chord 26.5 cm, path 27.5 cm (wiggle 1.038), maximum transverse excursion from its own chord 0.80 cm, rms 0.21 cm. For comparison the event's own 231 cm muon has wiggle 1.025 and the unowned pdg-211 prong 20022 has wiggle 1.144 with a 2.02 cm excursion, i.e. 20021's seed is straighter per unit length than the pion the reconstruction correctly refused to absorb. That is a vertex-attached MIP stem, and the brief's over-clustering rule names swallowing one explicitly. The genuinely shower-like members are the two downstream ones -- 20006 (9.4 cm, wiggle 1.157) and 20005 (10.3 cm, wiggle 1.126), running 20.8 to 37 cm from the vertex -- plus two on-axis stubs 62018 (0.5 cm at 39.7 cm / 21.5 deg) and 58014 (1.2 cm at 53.8 cm / 17.6 deg), both pass3_cone. Strip the seed and what is left is a compact EM object detached by ~21 cm, which is a perfectly ordinary photon conversion length; keep the seed and you have a 195 MeV photon that converted at 0.0 cm from the vertex, which is not a plausible conversion. MARK: 20021 OUT of its own shower 20021. That is deliberate and it is the whole finding -- it is the seed, so this is not a fringe stub being trimmed, and I would expect the owner to read it as 'the shower start is wrong', which is the same thing said the other way. THE READING I CANNOT EXCLUDE, and why this is likely rather than certain: if the whole object (seed plus 20006 plus 20005 plus the blob) is one interacting charged pion rather than a stem plus a converted photon, then the correct verdict is 'not an EM shower' and not over-clustering. I cannot separate a 2-MIP e+e- pair from a single pion by eye, and dE/dx is not on this display. NOT UNDER-CLUSTERED: the acceptance plot carries only the five member squares and NO non-member circle anywhere out to 65 cm and 27 deg, and the only unowned charge near the shower is 20022, the pion, which belongs out. PI0: no reco pi0 group (both pio_id -1) and none is possible -- the display auto-slotted 20021 + 20019, but BOTH of those start at the main vertex, so the vertex convention has no chord at all (kine_div prints theta '-' and m '-') and only the axis convention prices, at theta 142.4 deg -> 199.1 MeV. Two gammas that both sit on the vertex are not a pi0; the absence of a group here is correct.

[agent-bulk] mcp2k numucc_em WITH a reco pi0 group. 23 segments, 9 showers, 2 in scope (78026, 77020); the seven skipped (17029, 55007, 53005, 64016, 59011, 61013, 65017) are all under 20 MeV and 5.1 cm or shorter and I did not look at them individually, though 17029 matters below. drag_check both true, probe 105.1 px off centroid, not degenerate. r95 was 107.7 cm so the default vertex sweep is legible and I judged the vertex from it, no --vtx-span re-capture needed. VERTEX is good: the star sits where the 49.7 cm pdg-13 muon 17031 (correctly unowned) begins, with the 5.1 cm pdg-11 stub 17029 leaving the opposite side; at el+60 the same two-prong junction holds. LEADING SHOWER 78026 (159.6 MeV, 9 seg, 44.1 cm, conn 2, pio_id 0) is detached by 46.2 cm from the star -- a clean conversion gap -- and its member set is one direction and one apex: 78026 (18.8 cm seed), 78024 (4.9 cm) and 78025 (11.4 cm) at 16.7 cm / 1.8 deg, then 79027 (7.4 cm, a different cluster) at 35.8 cm / 7.3 deg. NOTHING IS MISSING: every non-member in the event lies at 129-177 deg to its axis, i.e. behind the start on the vertex side -- the muon at 173.7 deg, 77020's body at 173-177 deg, and the sub-MeV stubs at 153-172 deg. There is no grey charge anywhere in front of this shower, so I see no under-clustering, and the member set does not span two apexes or swallow a MIP stem, so no over-clustering either. THE ONE THING I WOULD LET THE OWNER REVERSE, and the reason this is likely rather than certain: five of the nine members are 0.2-0.5 cm pdg-13 specks absorbed by pass4_angle at 55.4, 68.4, 73.3, 76.4 and 79.3 cm from the shower start (101-125 cm from the vertex), on-axis at 4.4-17.3 deg. Reaching 79 cm downstream for a 160 MeV shower whose real body ends at 36 cm is a stretch; they carry negligible charge so they change no number, and they are individually spaced along the axis rather than a clump, which is why I did not mark them. This is the same pattern I let stand on evt399118 in wave 1, and I am being consistent rather than confident. SECOND SHOWER 77020 (63.1 MeV, 6 seg, 16.5 cm): a compact blob whose closest member is 5.1 cm from the star and which sits at 118 deg to the muon, so it is off the muon line rather than on it. Its members are contiguous 5.1-17.6 cm except one 0.5 cm pdg-13 speck (54006) at 57.9 cm / 13.8 deg from its start, the same over-reach pattern, unmarked for the same reason. Nothing unowned lies in front of 77020 either (all non-members 98-138 deg). PI0 -- and this is a pio_grp=1 event so the reco's own pairing is what I am checking: group 0 pairs 77020 + 78026 at 151.6 MeV, and I read the pairing as CONFIRMED. Both objects price as a pi0 in BOTH conventions -- axis convention theta 124.6 deg -> 177.7 MeV, vertex convention theta 98.1 deg -> 151.6 MeV, both flagged by the code as in the accept window -- and the pi0 panel shows the two gamma diamonds leaving the star in genuinely different directions, gamma1 up-range at about 40 deg above the muon and gamma2 down-range some 56 cm away. This is NOT the failure mode the brief warns about: neither gamma sits on the vertex (78026 is 46 cm out, 77020 is 5.1 cm out at a wide angle to the muon), and 5 cm is an ordinary conversion length, not a track root.
